entities.evidence: עַד חוֹבָה names Hobah as the endpoint of Abram’s pursuit.
לְדַמָּשֶׂק names Damascus as the city south of Hobah.

review.translation: [By night|2] [he|3] [and his servants|4] [split up|0] [against them|1], [and he defeated them|5] [and pursued them|6] [as far as|7] [Hobah|8], [which|9] [{is} north|10] [of Damascus|11].

analysis.evidence: הוּא וַעֲבָדָיו identifies Abram and his servants as the group that divided. עֲלֵיהֶם לַיְלָה places the action against their opponents at night, and וַיַּכֵּם then describes Abram striking them.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Niphal wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular. The verb precedes its compound subject and agrees with its first member, הוּא.
analysis.sense: Split into groups for an attack.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּחָלֵק עֲלֵיהֶם לַיְלָה, the suffix identifies the enemy against whom Abram and his servants divided their forces at night. The same enemy is the object of וַיַּכֵּם, “he struck them,” and וַיִּרְדְּפֵם, “he pursued them.”
analysis.morphology: The preposition עַל takes the form עֲלֵי־ before the third-person masculine plural pronominal suffix הֶם.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּחָלֵק עֲלֵיהֶם לַיְלָה, לַיְלָה tells when Abram and his servants divided their forces against the enemy.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute common noun used adverbially to indicate time.

analysis.evidence: הוּא refers to Abram. After the singular verb וַיֵּחָלֵק, the phrase הוּא וַעֲבָדָיו identifies those who divided up by night: “he and his servants.”
analysis.morphology: Independent third-person masculine singular personal pronoun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: he too; he and his company

analysis.evidence: הוּא וַעֲבָדָיו means “he and his servants.” The phrase identifies Abram and the men of his household who joined him in the night attack.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ means “and.” The noun is masculine plural construct with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix referring to Abram.

analysis.evidence: Abram and his servants attack by night. The same plural object appears in וַיִּרְדְּפֵם, “and he pursued them,” describing the pursuit of the defeated force as far as Hobah.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Hiphil wayyiqtol, third masculine singular, with Abram as subject. The third masculine plural object suffix ם refers to the opposing force.

analysis.evidence: וַיַּכֵּם says that Abram struck his opponents. The same plural object recurs in וַיִּרְדְּפֵם, and עַד חוֹבָה gives the endpoint of the chase.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third masculine singular, with Abram as subject. The third masculine plural object suffix refers to his opponents.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּרְדְּפֵם עַד חוֹבָה, “he pursued them as far as Hobah,” עַד marks Hobah as the endpoint of the pursuit. The following clause locates Hobah north of Damascus.
analysis.morphology: Simple preposition with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: as far as, up to, to (a place or person)

draft.change: Add Hobah as a place-name entry under nouns/, keyed by its own consonants because its derivation is uncertain.
draft.definition: Hobah, a place north of Damascus.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:15 names Hobah as the limit of Abram’s pursuit and locates it relative to Damascus.

analysis.evidence: וַיִּרְדְּפֵם עַד חוֹבָה means “he pursued them as far as Hobah.” The following clause, אֲשֶׁר מִשְּׂמֹאל לְדַמָּשֶׂק, locates Hobah north of Damascus.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun governed by עַד, “as far as.” The final ה belongs to the place name.
analysis.sense: The place north of Damascus where Abram’s pursuit ended.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause describing חוֹבָה. The phrase מִשְּׂמֹאל לְדַמָּשֶׂק gives its location, yielding “Hobah, which is north of Damascus.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add the geographical sense “north” to the noun שְׂמֹאל at word index 0.
draft.definition: The north side of a place, corresponding to the left when facing east.
draft.evidence: Gen.14.15 locates Hobah relative to Damascus. Ezk.16.46 pairs left and right to locate Samaria and Sodom relative to Jerusalem.

analysis.evidence: עַד חוֹבָה gives the endpoint of the pursuit. The relative clause אֲשֶׁר מִשְּׂמֹאל לְדַמָּשֶׂק locates Hobah on the left of Damascus, meaning north of it. Ezk.16.46 illustrates the same geographical use by placing Samaria on Jerusalem’s left and Sodom on its right.
analysis.morphology: The preposition מִן is prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun. Its נ assimilates to the initial שׂ, marked by dagesh.

draft.change: Add a place-name article keyed by the pointed lemma דַּמֶּשֶׂק. Its consonants דמשׂק distinguish it from the candidate root דמע.
draft.definition: Damascus, the city named as the capital of Aram.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:15 locates Hobah relative to Damascus. Isaiah 7:8 identifies Damascus as the head of Aram.

analysis.evidence: עַד חוֹבָה gives Hobah as the endpoint of the pursuit. The relative clause אֲשֶׁר מִשְּׂמֹאל לְדַמָּשֶׂק locates Hobah north of Damascus.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ introduces the place name דַּמֶּשֶׂק after מִשְּׂמֹאל. The name has the pausal form דַמָּשֶׂק at the end of the verse.
analysis.sense: The city of Damascus, used to locate Hobah.
